title: Reading-specific half-unit errors permit both local temperature slope signs in four US frog survey samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested how assumed temperature error groups affect local temperature slopes of recorded frog richness. We used 104,240 stops in 10,424 NAAMP runs in the Northeast and Midwest in 2001-2007 and 2008-2015. With run, site-window and order-window-year controls, half one reported unit permits both slope signs in each sample. The zero-numerator error multipliers are 0.023-0.060 for separate stops, 0.040-0.100 for equal readings within runs, and 0.220-0.876 for equal readings across each sample. An offset common to every stop on a run cancels exactly. Extra site-observer controls and run-specific order trends keep both signs possible. These are exact fixed-record possibility bounds under stated error sets, not confidence intervals, measured errors or causal climate effects. Decimal reports, unknown instrument precision, selected survey nights and one archive limit interpretation. This extends prior bird bounds with grouped errors and audits earlier frog results using the same records. Code, proof, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Raw records remain external.

display.caption: The multiplier of half one reported temperature unit that first permits a zero slope numerator. Each sample has its own possible errors. Values below one permit both signs under the stated bound. These are possibility thresholds, not measured errors or confidence limits. Run-common offsets cancel exactly and are not plotted.
